topStories.headline: Waxahachie Eyes New Stormwater Fee to Tackle Drainage Backlog
topStories.dek: City staff presented a proposal at the November 2 council meeting to create a dedicated stormwater utility fee that would fund long-deferred drainage improvement projects.
topStories.body:
Waxahachie city officials are exploring whether to establish a new stormwater utility fee that would generate a dedicated funding stream for drainage repairs and improvements across the city. The proposal was aired at the November 2 City Council meeting alongside a separate consultant recommendation that the city raise utility rates more broadly.

The city's Public Works and Development Engineering department has been working to modernize Waxahachie's stormwater system, which ultimately drains into Lake Waxahachie and Lake Bardwell — the community's primary drinking water sources. Officials have said that without a stable, earmarked revenue source, drainage projects regularly compete with other budget priorities and are pushed back.

No vote on the fee was taken at the November 2 meeting. The City Council holds its next regular session on Monday, November 16, at 7 p.m. at the Waxahachie Civic Center, 2000 Civic Center Lane, where the stormwater fee and broader utility rate proposals may advance. All council meetings are streamed live; agendas are posted at waxahachietx.gov.

topStories.headline: WHS Marching Band Takes 'Get to the Point' to UIL 6A State Championships
topStories.dek: Waxahachie High School's marching band and color guard competed at the UIL 6A State Marching Band Championship on November 9 and 10, capping a historic season for Waxahachie ISD's music programs.
topStories.body:
The Waxahachie High School marching band and color guard qualified for and competed at the UIL 6A State Marching Band Championship on November 9 and 10, 2026, performing their season show titled 'Get to the Point.' The state competition drew Class 6A programs from across Texas; Flower Mound High School took first place, followed by Hebron and Vandegrift.

The state appearance was part of a landmark year for Waxahachie ISD band programs. For the first time, all four WISD bands — WHS and the Coleman, Finley, and Howard junior high school ensembles — advanced to area competition simultaneously, according to the Waxahachie Sun.

Separately, the WHS Wind Ensemble advanced to the Class 6A state semifinals of the Texas Music Educators Association Honor Band Competition, one of 75 bands selected out of 229 that competed at the area level. The ensemble submitted recordings of works by John Philip Sousa, Walter Piston, and Paul Hindemith under the direction of band director Justin Bell, who noted the program had previously won the TMEA top honor in 2011 and 2017.

topStories.headline: Council Approves $350,000 Contract to Overhaul Parks Master Plan
topStories.dek: At its November 2 regular meeting, the City Council authorized a consulting agreement to produce an updated Parks and Recreation Master Plan, with a 2027 target for the finished document.
topStories.body:
The Waxahachie City Council voted at its November 2 regular meeting to approve a roughly $350,000 agreement with a planning consultant to update the city's Parks and Recreation Master Plan. The original plan dates to 2007 and established the guiding vision of 'Where Culture Meets Nature,' identifying the historic downtown, wooded creek corridors, and Lake Waxahachie as defining community assets.

City officials have flagged the update as overdue as Waxahachie's population has grown past 53,000 residents and development has spread across the city's 51 square miles. The new plan is expected to address priorities including expansion of the Waxahachie Creek Hike and Bike Trail system, additional neighborhood parks in developing areas, and improved pedestrian and bicycle links between parks and neighborhoods. A completion target of 2027 has been set.

The November 2 meeting also approved a site plan for a Brake Masters auto service shop and a repair contract for the roof of Waxahachie Municipal Airport. The council's next regular meeting is Monday, November 16, at 7 p.m. at the Waxahachie Civic Center.

events.title: 13th Annual Festival of Trees — Habitat for Humanity Fundraiser
events.location: First United Methodist Church, 505 W. Marvin, Waxahachie
events.description: Habitat for Humanity Ellis County hosts its annual Festival of Trees, featuring community-decorated trees, wreaths, and holiday items auctioned to support local homebuilding efforts. The event is open to the public on both days.

events.title: 26th Annual Ellis County Veterans Celebration
events.location: Waxahachie Civic Center, 2000 Civic Center Lane, Waxahachie
events.description: The annual ceremony honoring Ellis County veterans features patriotic music, tributes, and community recognition of those who have served in the United States Armed Forces. Organizers noted several additions to this year's program.

events.title: Waxahachie City Council Regular Meeting
events.location: Waxahachie Civic Center, 2000 Civic Center Lane, Waxahachie
events.description: The council's regular bi-monthly session; the proposed stormwater utility fee and the tabled Bent Tree Townhomes housing tax credit resolution are among items expected to return for consideration. Meetings stream live at waxahachietx.gov.

events.title: Ellis County Commissioners' Court Regular Meeting
events.description: The Commissioners' Court holds its regular monthly session. Recent agendas have included road closure updates and plat applications for unincorporated parts of the county.

events.title: Ellis County Turkey Trot
events.description: The annual Thanksgiving Day Turkey Trot returns to Waxahachie. Full details on start time, course, and registration are available through the City of Waxahachie Parks and Recreation event calendar at waxahachietx.gov.

moreNews.headline: Ellis County Road Closures Updated November 12
moreNews.body: Ellis County published its latest road closure list on November 12, 2026, covering roads across unincorporated parts of the county. Drivers in Garrett, Maypearl, Bardwell, and surrounding rural areas are encouraged to check elliscountytx.gov for the current list before traveling on county roads.

moreNews.headline: Commissioners' Court Called Special Meeting for November 13
moreNews.body: The Ellis County Commissioners' Court posted notice on November 5 of a special meeting scheduled for Friday, November 13, 2026, at 9:30 a.m. The public notice did not specify agenda items beyond the standard open-meeting posting. Minutes and any actions taken will be published at elliscountytx.gov following the meeting.
